status: Local, not committed or published; teaching-only addition. Accepted answers unchanged.

groups.text: Tras takes the event directly: tras la clase. Después can stand alone or take de: después de la clase. Luego also means later/next and can take de; entonces can mean at that time or introduce a conclusion.
Empezar and comenzar both mean begin and take a + infinitive. Comenzar tends toward formal/written use and empezar toward informal/spoken use, with regional variation—not a strict division.
Saber is for facts and know-how: saber nadar. Conocer is for acquaintance or familiarity: conocer a Ana. Entender and comprender both express understanding; there is no mandatory shallow/deep split.

Pensar is thinking about something; creer is taking something as true; sentir covers sensations and feelings. They can overlap when expressing opinions. Considerar can mean examining an option or judging something; parecer expresses an impression.
Ser identifies or classifies: Ana es médica. Estar presents a state: Ana está cansada. The distinction is not simply permanent versus temporary.
In the basic spatial contrast, este is near the speaker, ese near the listener, and aquel distant from both. Their time and conversational-reference uses extend beyond physical distance.
Por can give a cause: por la lluvia. Para can identify a recipient: un regalo para Ana, or a purpose: para aprender. Both have other uses, so this is not an exhaustive cause/purpose rule.
Dejar las llaves means leave the keys behind; salir de casa means exit the house; irse means depart/go away. Dejar also means let someone do something, and dejar de + infinitive means stop doing it.

Lograr emphasizes achieving a sought result; conseguir also means attain/get. Both take a direct infinitive for succeeding in an action. Obtener means obtain but does not fit that same infinitive construction. Recibir is receiving; tener is having.
Aún and todavía both mean continuing still. Ya can mean already; ya no means no longer. Ahora means now. Aun without the accent has other uses, including even.
Tener expresses having: tener un libro. Haber forms compound tenses (he comido) and existential hay (there is/are). Existir means exist; these are different uses hidden by English have/be.
Ir means go; venir means come toward the speaker's location. Llegar emphasizes arrival, entrar/salir crossing inside/outside, and volver returning. Volver a + infinitive means do again.
Quedar can describe what is left: quedan tres entradas. Seguir can mean follow or continue. Mantener means keep or sustain something in a state; mantenerse can mean remain in that state.
Llevar carries or takes something along; tomar can mean take/grasp or drink. Poner places it; dejar can leave it there. Dar gives something; recibir receives it.

Hacer is broad do/make; realizar carries out an action. Crear emphasizes bringing something into existence; producir an output or result; convertir en changes something into something else. Some uses overlap.
Ver is visual perception; mirar directs your gaze or attention. Both can translate watch in suitable contexts. Sentir concerns sensations and feelings rather than specifically directing your eyes.
Mostrar and enseñar can mean show something. Presentar also puts something before someone, but presentar a una persona means introduce a person; enseñar also means teach.
Decir expresses particular content; hablar is speaking or conversation. Contar can count items or tell a story. Llamar can call by phone, summon or name; explicar makes something understandable.
Preguntar asks for information: preguntar la hora. Pedir requests something or an action: pedir agua. Asking what something is and asking to receive it are different.
Buscar is looking for something; encontrar is finding or encountering it. Conocer a alguien is knowing or becoming acquainted with a person.
Querer expresses wanting or affection. Esperar can mean wait, hope or expect, depending on context; waiting for someone does not simply mean wanting them to arrive.
Poder expresses ability or possibility; deber obligation or owing. Permitir and dejar overlap when giving permission. These are different meanings even when English uses can, may or must.
Tratar de + infinitive means try to do something; tratar de + a topic can mean be about it. Considerar examines or judges something; hablar de means speak about it.
De can express possession, origin or material. Desde explicitly marks a starting point. For spans, de…a, desde…a and desde…hasta are all valid; since Monday is desde el lunes.
A can name a destination; hacia highlights direction toward it. Para can also express destination/direction. A destination does not by itself assert that someone arrived.
En means in/on/at according to context. Sobre can mean on/above or about a topic. Dentro means inside and uses de before a named place; entre means between/among.
Antes is earlier in time: antes de la clase. Ante directly introduces being before/in the presence of someone or facing something: ante el juez.
Durante takes a period/event noun: durante la clase. Mientras introduces simultaneous activity: mientras leo. Mientras que can be temporal or contrastive; cuando locates an event in time.
También adds a parallel participant or fact: yo también. Además introduces further information and also appears in además de. They overlap, but sentence placement and emphasis may differ.
Porque gives a cause. Causal como introduces a background reason first; causal pues follows what it explains. Pues, entonces and luego can also introduce consequences or inferences in other uses.
Pero adds a contrast: pequeño pero cómodo. Sino replaces something denied: no té, sino café. Aunque introduces a concession: aunque llueva (even if it rains).

Relative que can refer to people or things; quien refers to people. El cual/la cual form relative expressions. Qué and cómo carry accents in questions and exclamations; que also introduces statements.

Subject, unstressed object and after-preposition forms differ: yo, me and mí. Lo is a direct-object form; le an indirect-object form, with regional qualifications. Se also has several uses beyond reflexive oneself.
Mío refers to me, nuestro to us, and tuyo to tú/vos. Suyo can refer to él/ella/ellos/ellas or usted/ustedes; context identifies the owner. These forms agree with what is owned.
Accents can distinguish grammatical roles: el (the) / él (he), si (if) / sí (yes), and que (that) / qué (what?). They are not freely interchangeable spellings.

Un is the article before a masculine noun; uno can stand alone as the number or an indefinite person. Solo as an adverb means only; único is an adjective meaning sole/unique. Adjectival solo can mean alone.

Todo covers the whole; cada distributes over members or intervals (cada tres días). Alguno selects an unspecified member; cualquiera allows free choice; ninguno means none. Varios and algunos overlap without a fixed numerical cutoff.

Muy modifies noncomparative adjectives/adverbs: muy alto. Mucho modifies actions or comparatives: trabaja mucho, mucho mejor; it also quantifies nouns. Tan goes before adjectives/adverbs; tanto can modify an action.
Bueno is adjectival good; bien describes doing something well and can also intensify an adjective. Mejor can compare either good or well. Their grammatical roles matter, not just the English gloss.
Grande describes size broadly; alto height; largo length or duration. Mayor can mean larger/older, but also grown-up or elderly. Pequeño can mean small or young, depending on context.

Mismo identifies the same person or thing; propio emphasizes belonging to someone; otro adds or distinguishes another; único means sole/unique. These are separate senses despite some emphatic overlap.
Tiempo measures duration; vez counts occurrences; hora can be a 60-minute unit or a specified time. Momento can be a brief interval or a period characterized by an event. Día names a day.

Trabajo includes work, employment and a produced result. Obra often names a created work, including art or construction. Estudio can mean studying, an analytical work or a studio; trabajar is the verb.
Persona is an individual; gente is generally collective people. Niño describes age; hijo a relationship to parents, even for an adult. Some American varieties also use gente for individual people.
Forma can mean physical shape or a way of doing something. Manera and modo also express a way/manner. Tipo and clase instead classify things into kinds.

Estado and situación overlap for condition/circumstances; there is no strict internal/external split. Estado also names a political state. Caso can name a particular matter, occurrence or investigation.
Lugar is a location; parte a portion; lado a side; punto can be a dot, point or location. Centro is the middle; nivel a level or degree. Broader place senses overlap, so context matters.
Grupo is a collection of people or things. Equipo can be a team organized for an activity or equipment for a purpose. Conjunto can mean a collection and also specifically a sports team.

País is a country/territory; estado can be a political organization or a federal state; gobierno its governing body. Nacional, público, social and político describe different relationships, not one interchangeable idea.
Proceso describes successive stages; desarrollo their development or unfolding; cambio something becoming different; proyecto a planned undertaking. Development does not always mean improvement.

Historia can mean history or a story. Relación can mean a connection or an account/list; cuenta can mean an account, bill or calculation. Tema is subject matter; información communicated knowledge; palabra a word.
Vida is the noun life; vivir means be alive or reside; existir means exist and can also refer to being alive. Residence is a particular vivir sense, not the whole meaning of life/existence.
Siempre means always; nunca means never. Cada distributes over members and marks repeated intervals, as in cada tres días (every three days).
No negates; ni joins negatives or can mean not even; sin expresses without. Y adds; o offers alternatives and sometimes alternative names for the same thing.
Desde marks a starting point; hasta an endpoint; durante a period; entre between/among. Hasta also has an even sense, and its time use varies regionally in some constructions.
Medio can name a means used to achieve something. Sistema is an organized system or method; manera/forma how something is done. Así means in this way.
Primero and segundo mark positions in a sequence; último its end. Antes and después express relative time/order. Related meanings do not make the different grammatical forms interchangeable.
Con can express accompaniment (con Ana) or an instrument. Por can express a means or channel. English with/by needs a specific relationship to choose between them.
Hoy is this calendar day; ahora this moment/current time. Both can also describe a broader present period, so the contrast is not absolute in every sentence.
Recordar brings or keeps something in memory and can mean remind someone. Saber means know. Recordar algo takes its object directly; acordarse de algo uses de.
